zh adds 「一口气」 (in one go / in one breath), which is not in jp 「丸ごと一つ食べた」 or in en "ate a fresh apple whole" — it shifts the point from wholeness to speed, which is precisely the sense 丸ごと does not carry.

The target is swallowed by the frozen adverbial 念のため: both en ("just to be sure") and zh (「以防万一」) translate the idiom as a unit, so 念 itself is rendered by nothing in either gloss and the learner sees no evidence of its "care/attention" meaning.

zh 「在一家房产公司工作了」 with sentence-final 了 reads as "worked at a real-estate company (for a while / and that's over)", whereas jp 就職した and en "got a job at a real estate company" denote entering employment. 进了一家房地产公司工作／就职于… would match.
Connotation drift: jp 噂 and en "rumor" are neutral, but zh 「谣言」 specifically means a false or malicious rumor. 传闻／流言 would keep the neutral reading the Japanese has.

misleadingCards.why: Gloss line is only 'cheerful, lighthearted', but 気軽にご質問ください uses the 'feel free / without hesitation / casually' sense. Nothing on the card explains why a word meaning 'cheerful' appears before 'please ask questions'.
Gloss line is 'anyhow, in various ways', but the sentence uses the 'apt to / tends to' sense (忘れがちだ). A learner would read 兎角 as 'anyhow' and the sentence's 'tends to' would be unexplained.

Gloss line is 'shrinking back, being baffled', but the sentence means being fed up/exasperated with a boastful story. A learner would take 辟易 as intimidated or confused; the disgust/fed-up sense the sentence needs is absent.
Sentence is 花を愛でたい 'want to admire the flowers' — the verb 愛でる + たい. The gloss line only gives めでたい 'happy, auspicious', a different word entirely; nothing on the card explains 'admire'.
持てる力をすべて発揮 uses 持てる as 'the strength one possesses'. Gloss line gives only 'to be well liked, to be popular', which cannot explain the sentence at all.
Sentence is the sewing sense — basting/tacking fabric temporarily. The gloss line offers 'to train, to discipline, to plant', none of which explains 仮に仕付ける in 裁縫.

Gloss is nouns 'buried property, treasure trove', but the sentence is 天然ガスが埋蔵されている — buried natural-resource reserves used verbally. Neither 'deposits/reserves' nor the verbal 'to be deposited underground' sense is in the gloss line; 'treasure trove' actively points the learner away from natural gas.

Sentence is 体を労りたい = take good care of one's body, but the gloss line only offers 'to pity, to console'. Neither covers caring for/being gentle with one's health — the learner would read it as pitying their own body.

Sentence uses 煙る for distant mountains looking hazy/misty in rain, but the gloss line only says 'to smoke, to smolder'. The haze/blurred-by-moisture sense is absent, so the definition does not explain the sentence.

Gloss line is purely military ('war potential, military capability'), but the sentence uses 戦力 figuratively for a new player being a valuable asset to a sports team — that sense is absent, so the definition does not explain the sentence.

Gloss line offers only 'to collect, to extort, to appoint', but the sentence uses 取り立てるほどの (worth special mention) — the 'single out / mention specially' sense is missing, so none of the three glosses parses the sentence.

Sentence uses the formulaic apologetic preface 恐れ入りますが = "excuse me / sorry to trouble you"; the line offers only "filled with awe, amazed, obliged", none of which explains the polite-request usage in front of the learner.
Sentence is 台風が接近する恐れがある — the "risk / danger that something bad may happen" sense; the gloss line gives only the emotion (fear, horror, anxiety), so it does not explain ~恐れがある.

Sentence is 大きな重い棚を据えた = installing/setting a heavy shelf firmly in place; both glosses are narrowed by parentheticals to unrelated collocations ("to set (table)", "to lay (foundation)"), so the line does not explain the sentence.
Sentence is a neighborhood 騒動 = a commotion/disturbance, but the line offers only "rebellion, mutiny, riot", which pushes the learner to read it as a violent uprising next door.

Sentence uses the fixed phrase いざという時 = "should the need arise / in an emergency", but the gloss line offers only the interjection sense "now, come"; a learner cannot get "when the time comes" out of that.
